nodes.label: Manual Stripe-migration prompt email to an operator
Super-admin-only send gate (app_users.is_super_admin), verified with the service-role client
Preview action returns prefilled recipient/subject/body so the admin composer can be populated before sending
Rationale: ignore the branding library's global default so support@drive-247.com is never prefilled as the operator recipient
Rationale in the email copy: Stripe now requires regional rental platforms to settle through an operator-owned account (managed to own account move)
Migration copy promises 100 free credits once both onboarding steps are complete
Branding wrap is best-effort — an unbranded plain-HTML fallback still sends rather than failing the operator's click
On-demand Pay-As-You-Go payment reminder (operator 'Send reminder' button on the rental detail page)
Admin override: bypasses all cron cadence gating except open-invoice and customer-email sanity checks
Stripe pay-link rotation: safely expire the prior reminder's Checkout session before minting a fresh one
Pre-create a Pending payments row keyed by stripe_checkout_session_id so process-pending-payment can find the session
Rationale: outstanding must come from ledger remaining_amount, not gross accruals — a partial FIFO payment leaves the accrual 'open' and would re-bill paid days
Rationale: this is a FORK of the shared email renderer with the plate-privacy guard absent, so hide_vehicle_registration must be applied at composition time
Always write a payg_reminder_log row so every operator click is auditable even when the email send fails
Rationale: non-2xx reserved for genuine server faults so the UI can distinguish 'email failed but attempt logged' from 'function crashed'
Rationale: a failed manual send must not advance the reminder pointer, otherwise it would push the next auto-cron window back
Rationale: email-template helpers vendored inline so MCP deploys need not upload the 34KB shared module
Pay-As-You-Go automated payment-reminder cron
Reminder cadence gate: per-rental override then tenant default then 4-day fallback, anchored to last send or activation
Rationale: historical bug — the cadence gate was hardcoded to a 5-minute 'TEST MODE' constant that was never reverted, so every daily tick passed and customers were reminded daily
Safe-expire of the prior reminder's Checkout session — never cancel a session with a payment_intent already in flight
Rationale: on a Stripe retrieve/expire error do NOT stamp expired_at — a live stale link cannot double-bill because payg_settle_invoice is idempotent and FIFO routes excess to the next open accrual
Checkout metadata (payg_accrual_id + target_categories) drives the webhook and DB-trigger settlement chain that flips the right invoice to paid
Rationale: sum ledger remaining_amount, not gross accruals — an accrual stays 'open' until every category for the day is drained
Pre-create a Pending payments row mirroring create-checkout-session, without which process-pending-payment 404s and captured money never lands in the DB
only_rental_id sandbox scoping — a Time Machine dispatch can never touch another tenant's rentals
Booking-app origin resolution for Stripe success/cancel URLs: BOOKING_BASE_URL override then {slug}.{BOOKING_BASE_DOMAIN}
Rationale: forked renderer without the plate-privacy guard — hide_vehicle_registration is applied by blanking vehicle_reg at composition
Rationale: template helpers kept in-file and byte-interchangeable with _shared/email-template-service.ts so either import path works at deploy time
Per-tenant payg_reminder email template override from Settings, with an inline default fallback
New PAYG charges are minted on the tenant's CURRENT platform account (managed = legacy UK keys, own = UAE keys)
increment_payg_reminder_count RPC — advances the rental's reminder count and last-sent stamp, with a direct UPDATE fallback
Customer notification that a manually-reviewed payment was declined
Copy asserts 'the associated rental booking has been cancelled' — this function only emails; the cancellation itself happens in the caller
tenant_id is back-filled from the payments row when the caller omits it, so branding and currency still resolve
Operator alert that a payment is pending manual approve/reject
Operator email gated on the tenant's 'payments' notification preference and routed to the configured notification recipient
CTA deep-links to {slug}.portal.drive-247.com/payments?status=pending so the operator lands on the pending queue
Manual payment verification loop: operator is alerted, approves or rejects, and the customer is told the outcome
Operational reminder digest: fans pending reminders out to in-app notifications plus one email digest per admin
Per-admin dedupe by matching notifications.metadata.reminder_id before inserting a new in-app notification
Reminder state transition pending to sent, stamped with last_sent_at and logged as a reminder_actions row
Gotcha: admin recipients are selected by role alone with no tenant filter, so every tenant's admins receive every tenant's reminders
Gotcha: digest branding is taken from the FIRST pending reminder's tenant, so a mixed-tenant batch is branded with the wrong operator
Reminder object_type maps to a portal deep link (Vehicle, Rental, Customer, Fine, Integration)
Vehicle-return reminder cron — finds rentals nearing end_date within the tenant's return_reminder_hours window
rentals.return_reminder_sent_at is the idempotency key that prevents a second reminder for the same rental
Urgency escalation from hours-until-return: return_24h, return_today (<=12h), overdue (<=0h)
only_rental_id sandbox scoping for Time Machine dispatches, hard-restricting the cron to one rental
Gotcha: the stamp is written only after notify-rental-reminder returns, so a notify failure leaves the rental eligible on the next tick
Branded 'rental agreement ready to sign' email carrying the BoldSign signing link
Rationale: the esign route pre-fetches the signing link after document creation and passes it in, avoiding a redundant BoldSign API call
BoldSign test-mode banner declaring the document not legally binding, driven by the per-rental boldsign_mode
WhatsApp delivery of the e-signature signing link to a customer
Two independent WhatsApp transports coexist: this uses _shared/whatsapp-client.ts (Meta Cloud API) while send-tenant-whatsapp uses Twilio
Staff-to-customer outbound SMS from the unified inbox, sent on the tenant's own Twilio credentials
Second path for numbers with no customer record — replies land in sms_unknown_threads / sms_unknown_messages instead of a chat channel
After every send, chat_channels.last_message_at and last_channel are updated so the inbox list orders and labels correctly
Tenant resolution: staff are pinned to their own app_users.tenant_id; only a super admin may supply tenantId in the request body
Gotcha: the Twilio send happens before the DB insert, so an insert failure leaves a message delivered to the customer but missing from the thread
Sales strategy-call email sequence for inbound operator leads
Five-stage sequence: confirmation, 24h reminder, 1h reminder, attended follow-up, no-show follow-up
Documented gap: no scheduler is wired — reminders and follow-ups must be triggered externally once call_time is known
Platform-level hardcoded brand block (UK Covent Garden address, placeholder unsubscribe URL, founder name, Calendly links) with TODOs to move to env
Idempotent send ledger: upsert on (contact_request_id, email_type) so a stage is recorded once
Tenant welcome email carrying the Stripe Connect onboarding link and first-login portal credentials
Sends through a raw SigV4-signed AWS SES request rather than the shared Resend service, so it carries no tenant branding
Admin email and temporary password rendered in plain text inside the email body
When AWS is unconfigured the function returns success:true with simulated:true — callers cannot tell a real send from a no-op
Thin per-tenant Twilio SMS sender used by other notification functions
Unconfigured Twilio returns success:false / skipped:true instead of an error, so a caller's notification flow is never broken by a missing integration
Thin per-tenant Twilio WhatsApp sender used by other notification functions
Two soft-skip gates (no Twilio credentials, no WhatsApp sender number) both return skipped:true rather than failing the caller
Toll-charge statement email with a single pay-now button

Rationale: money stays on the proven checkout path — the caller mints the pay-link via create-checkout-session (targetCategories ['Fine']) and passes only the URL, so this function never touches payments or the ledger
Deliberately JWT-protected (staff-invoked) and intentionally NOT added to the verify_jwt=false allow-list
Portal staff welcome email with temporary login credentials and the tenant portal URL
Calls the Resend REST API directly with a FROM_EMAIL env default (onboarding@resend.dev) instead of the shared resend-service tenant-slug sender
Temporary password rendered in plain text inside the email body, paired with a forced password change on first login
Re-implements tenant branding inline (reads tenants colours/logo/slug itself) rather than using getTenantBranding / wrapWithBrandedTemplate
Six-digit email OTP for customer verification and password reset, with a 15-minute expiry
One live code per email+tenant: prior codes are deleted and globally expired codes swept on every issue
Gotcha: the delete keys tenant_id on empty string when absent while the insert writes NULL, so tenant-less codes are never superseded
The OTP is placed in the email subject line as well as the body, so it is visible in notification previews
Staff-to-customer outbound WhatsApp from the unified inbox, on the tenant's own Twilio WhatsApp number
24-hour session-window handling: with no recent inbound customer message, an approved content template is auto-sent to reopen the window before the free-form message
The template opener is sent silently and never written to chat_channel_messages, so the visible thread shows only the operator's real message
Failure messages tell the operator exactly what to fix (customer must message first, or create an approved template in Settings > Messaging > WhatsApp)
Legacy org_settings read/write API with audit logging
Write allowlist — unknown keys are dropped before the PostgREST update so a stray field cannot fail the whole save
Rationale: dark_logo_url and auth_logo_url are deliberately NOT in the allowlist — org_settings has only logo_url; those two columns live on tenants and are kept in step by use-tenant-branding.ts
60-second module-scope settings cache, busted on every successful write
Treats org_settings as a single global row (limit(1).single()) and auto-seeds defaults when none exists — a pre-multi-tenant assumption
Audit tenant resolution chain: frontend _tenant_id, then org_settings.tenant_id, then app_users.tenant_id, then tenants lookup by org_id
Gotcha: timezone is validated against four hardcoded zones and currency against USD/EUR/GBP only, narrower than tenants.currency_code elsewhere in the platform
Audit-log outcome is leaked back into the settings response as _audit_error/_audit_log_id/_audit_skipped debug fields
Two clients on purpose: the anon client carries the caller's JWT so RLS still applies to the settings write, while the service client does the audit insert
Force-logout every user of a tenant by revoking their auth sessions
Rationale: auth.admin.signOut(user_id) expects an access-token JWT, not a user id, so the previous implementation failed on every user and signed nobody out
GoTrue exposes no admin 'logout by user-id' endpoint, so sessions are deleted over the direct Postgres connection injected as SUPABASE_DB_URL
Belt-and-suspenders sweep of orphaned auth.refresh_tokens not covered by the session-delete cascade
Gotcha: no JWT or super-admin check in the handler — any caller who can reach the function can evict a whole tenant's staff
